title: agent-parser: replace the WASM SQLite driver with a native one
description:
agent-parser reads OpenCode databases through `github.com/ncruces/go-sqlite3`, which runs SQLite as WASM. Replace it with a native driver.

The driver is registered in one place, `opencode.go`, and used through `database/sql` (`sql.Open("sqlite3", dsn)`). agent-watcher names the module in `go.mod` for its tests and inherits the runtime dependency through agent-parser, so its `go.mod` and test fixtures change too. devhost has no SQLite dependency today and gains this one when it adopts agent-watcher.

The driver choice has a build constraint. devhost release artifacts are cross-compiled with `CGO_ENABLED=0` (`apps/devhost/scripts/buildReleaseArtifacts.ts`).
- A cgo driver such as `github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3` does not work in those builds, so choosing one means changing the devhost release flow to cross-compile with a C toolchain per platform. That needs explicit approval.
- `modernc.org/sqlite` is pure Go with no WASM and no cgo, so it fits the existing builds. It is the default choice unless a measured reason rules it out. Confirm this before starting.

Details to check:
- The driver name and DSN syntax differ between drivers, including the options that open the OpenCode database read-only.
- Reads must stay safe while OpenCode is writing to the database.
- Compare binary size, startup time and query time against the current driver. The full agent-watcher scanner probe, with the WASM driver, built to 4.5 MB.
- Update the `rust` counterpart only if it shares the dependency.

Done when agent-parser and agent-watcher pass their tests on the new driver, `go mod tidy` removes the WASM modules from both, and a `CGO_ENABLED=0` build reads a real OpenCode database.
